title: Connected components and islands
summary: Restart a traversal from every unvisited vertex to count the pieces of a graph.
hints: A single BFS/DFS only covers what is reachable from one start. To cover the whole graph, loop `for s := range len(g)` and start a new traversal whenever `s` is not visited yet. Each time you start one, you have found one new component.

Write a small helper that floods from a vertex/cell and marks everything it reaches. For `CountComponents` it needs to return nothing; for `LargestIsland` have it return how many cells it marked. Use whichever traversal you like, BFS with a queue slice avoids deep recursion.

For the grid, reuse the direction-table idea from the maze exercise. Keep a `visited` grid of the same shape (`[][]bool`). Do not try to write `'0'` into the grid itself: a string is immutable in Go and the slice you were given belongs to the caller. Only cells equal to `'1'` count as land.
